findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or implement in the plan) the required parser surgery in `edit_cli`: add a boolean-flag branch that recognises `--review` without consuming a value (`i += 1` only), explicitly noting that the current parsing loop has no such pathway (lines 534-540 of composer.py).
evidence: Plan: 'accept `--review` as a non-field flag'

composer.py:534-539: `elif arg.startswith('--'): name = arg[2:]; if i + 1 >= n: print(f'Error: --{name} requires a value', ...); return 1; val = rest[i + 1]; i += 2` — no branch for a boolean flag that consumes no value
No `if name == 'review': review_flag = True; i += 1; continue` or equivalent pattern exists in the parser
findings.finding: The plan asserts that `--review` can be accepted as a 'non-field flag' in `edit_cli`, but `edit_cli`'s existing arg-parsing loop (lines 534–539) has NO boolean/valueless flag pathway: every `--flag` form (without `=`) unconditionally reads the next token as a value (`val = rest[i + 1]; i += 2`). A bare `--review` will either error ('--review requires a value') if it is the last argument, or silently consume the following token as its value. The plan does not acknowledge that the parser loop needs structural surgery to support a boolean flag.
findings.location: Approach section ('accept `--review` as a non-field flag'); src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:534-540
scenarios: A developer implementing the plan adds `elif name == 'review': ...` after the unknown-field check but before the else, not noticing that `val = rest[i+1]` has already consumed the next arg — causing silent misparse when `--review` precedes a field flag.
The test suite stubs review_plan but invokes edit_cli with `['ticket-id', '--review']` as the last token; the CLI returns exit 1 with 'requires a value' rather than running the review.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section, add: 'Because `edit_cli`'s parser always reads `rest[i+1]` as a flag value, add a boolean-flag guard before the `_EDIT_FIELDS` check: `if name == "review": review_flag = True; i += 1; continue` (consuming only the flag token itself, not a value).'

findings.finding: The claim --review mechanism is specified as 'on a plan-review CommandError run review_plan(sign=True)'. `plan_review_precheck` (claim.py:133) only raises `CommandError` when the gate is ENABLED and the attestation is missing/stale. findings.finding: The decision rule for which `CommandError` subtypes from `plan_review_precheck` should trigger `review_plan` in `claim --review` is unspecified: the gate raises `CommandError` for both recoverable cases (missing/stale attestation — appropriate to auto-review) and non-recoverable cases (ticket exempt, gate disabled returning None — inappropriate to auto-review), and the plan does not co-locate the discrimination rule.
findings.location: Approach section — `claim --review` description: 'at the precheck call (src/rebar/_commands/claim.py:133), on a plan-review CommandError run review_plan(sign=True)'
scenarios: A new precheck failure mode is added (e.g., dependency not reviewed) that raises CommandError — claim --review auto-triggers an LLM review that cannot resolve the actual block.
An implementor catches all CommandErrors from plan_review_precheck and always invokes review_plan, producing a multi-minute billable review for a non-attestation block.

findings.finding: `rebar.llm.review_plan` returns a `dict[str, Any]`, not an exit code — the plan's statement 'pass through its exit code (0 PASS / 1 BLOCK / 2 INDETERMINATE / 11 retryable)' is an unbacked assertion about the function's return type. The exit-code mapping lives in the private CLI helper `_disposition_exit_code` at `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:92`, which also has stderr side-effects. The plan leaves unspecified how `edit_cli` will perform this mapping.
findings.location: Approach section, item (1): 'invoke rebar.llm.review_plan(ticket_id, sign=True) in the foreground and pass through its exit code'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach (1): 'Map the dict verdict to an exit code via `_cli._llm_commands._disposition_exit_code(result, indeterminate_code=2)` (the same mapping the `review-plan` CLI uses at line 536) and return that code from `edit_cli`.'

findings.finding: The plan says `edit --review` should 'invoke rebar.llm.review_plan(ticket_id, sign=True) in the foreground and pass through its exit code (0 PASS / 1 BLOCK / 2 INDETERMINATE / 11 retryable).' However, `rebar.llm.review_plan()` returns a dict, not an integer. The exit-code derivation logic — including the critical exit-11 retryable case (PASS with a failed attestation persistence) — lives in `_disposition_exit_code()` in `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:92-145`. An implementer who naively derives the exit code from `result['verdict']` alone will silently drop the retryable-sign-failure path (exit 11 instead of 0), diverging from `rebar review-plan`'s behavior.
findings.location: Approach section — '(1) rebar edit <id> ... --review' / src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:398 / src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:92
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section, replace 'pass through its exit code' with 'pass through the integer exit code derived by calling `_disposition_exit_code(result, indeterminate_code=2)` on the returned verdict dict, matching the mapping used by `rebar review-plan`.'

findings.finding: The plan asserts that `rebar.llm.review_plan(ticket_id, sign=True)` returns an exit code (0/1/2/11) that can be directly propagated, but the actual function returns a `dict[str, Any]` containing a `verdict` string and `coverage` dict; the exit-code mapping is performed by `_disposition_exit_code()` in `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:92-145`. Both `edit --review` and `claim --review` are specified to 'pass through its exit code,' which requires calling this CLI-layer helper (or reimplementing the mapping) — an unverified capability the plan treats as a library guarantee.
